# menus


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A host describes its menu bar as data: a list of menus, each with a
title and a list of rows. This module defines the row types, and the
small part of a keymap a menu needs to read. They are plain dataclasses
that do not import pywebview or AppKit, so a host can build and test its
menu table on any machine. `kavacha.window` turns the table into a
native menu bar on macOS.

### The rows

[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
is a row that runs one of the host’s actions, named by `action`. When
the user chooses it, the window calls the host’s `on_action` with that
name. A
[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
with no action is a separator line, which is why `action` has a default.
`kind` is either empty or `warn`. `warn` marks a row the host may want
to draw as destructive, such as one that discards changes; kavacha
passes it through without acting on it, and refuses any other value.

### MenuItem

``` python
def MenuItem(
    action:str='', kind:str=''
)->None:
```

*One action in a menu. A blank action is a separator.*

``` python
MenuItem('open_folder'), MenuItem()
```

[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) is a row
that AppKit already knows how to handle, such as Cut, Copy, Paste and
Select All, so the host does not handle it at all. The row names an
AppKit selector, such as `cut:`. The menu sends that selector along
AppKit’s responder chain, the chain of objects that starts at whatever
has keyboard focus, and the first one that understands it acts. `key`
and `mods` give the row’s shortcut directly, because a row like this has
no entry in the host’s keymap.

[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) is a row
that runs a JavaScript expression in the focused window, for small jobs
such as reloading the page that need no action of their own.

### Js

``` python
def Js(
    title:str, expr:str

```

*A row that runs the JavaScript expression `expr` in the focused
window.*

``` python
Std('Cut', 'cut:', 'x'), Js('Reload', 'location.reload()')
```

### Key bindings

A menu shows each action’s label and shortcut, and the host keeps both
in its keymap. kavacha does not read the keymap itself. The host
supplies a lookup function that takes an action name and returns a
[`Binding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding),
or `None` for an action it does not know. A
[`Binding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)
holds the action’s chords, its label, and its scope, meaning where the
binding applies; only bindings with the scope `global` become menu
shortcuts. A dict’s `get` method is the simplest lookup, as in the
example.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/kavacha/blob/main/kavacha/menus.py#L38"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Binding

``` python
def Binding(
    keys:tuple=(), label:str='', scope:str='global'
)->None:
```

*What a menu row reads from the host’s keymap: the chords, the label,
and where it applies.*

``` python
keys = {'save': Binding(('mod+s',), 'Save'), 'find': Binding(('mod+f',), scope='editor')}
keys.get('save'), keys.get('nothing')
```

`bound` is true when the binding has at least one chord. It is worked
out from `keys` instead of being stored, so an unbound action is just
[`Binding()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)
and the two can never disagree.

[`kavacha.window.menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
takes the menu table and the lookup function together. kavacha ships no
default table for either, because what belongs on an app’s File menu is
up to the app.
